world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1913. The Languages of Borneo. Sarawak Museum Journal 1(4): 1-196.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Milikin/Remun: Milikin appears only as a locality note (p. 8: 'On tributary of Sadong River.. a mixture of Land and Sea Dayaks') and as a column in the comparative vocabularies (from Boult 1910, 1-page MS, bibliography no. 248). The single 'stress' remark (p. 14, 'a stronger stress on the last word of a sentence') is about Mantangai Ngaju, not Milikin.

sources.citation: Claudia Vica Bandan & Norazuna Norahim. 2023. Kajian Awal Kekerabatan Bahasa Remun dan Iban Undop (A Preliminary Study of Linguistic Affiliation between the Remun language and Undop Iban language). Journal of Borneo-Kalimantan 9(1): 13-25.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 'Perbezaan Ciri Fonologi Bahasa Iban Remun dan Iban Undop' (pp. 21-22) gives a 6-vowel /a e ə i o u/ and 19-consonant inventory with distribution, /r/ -> /ɣ/, h-loss, final glottal stop, vowel sequences /ai au ua/; explicitly 'penelitian awal sahaja kerana keterbatasan data'. No tekanan/stress. Lexicostatistics: 94.7% cognate with Iban Undop, treated as a dialect of Iban.

sources.citation: Chong Shin, Remmy Gedat & Mohammed Azlan Mis. 2019. Bahasa Remun di Negeri Sarawak: Kajian Perbandingan dengan Bahasa Iban. GEMA Online Journal of Language Studies 19(4): 203-218. doi:10.17576/gema-2019-1904-11
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The phonological analysis (ANALISIS DATA, pp. 210-215) is confined to two phonemes: r is /ɣ/ in Remun vs /r/ in Iban, and s is /h/ word-finally in Remun vs /s/ in Iban; 150-item lexical comparison (82% similar). No occurrence of tekanan/stress/aksen/intonasi in the text.
